writeup: TIC 459533211 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.0658 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 8.84%, with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 185.4 in the box-least-squares periodogram search. Pixel-level image analysis using difference imaging confirmed the signal near the target location, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 96.9, though with a centroid offset of 1.2 arcsec. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel target. While the machine-learning model assigned this candidate a screening score of 0.34, the data passed all automated quality checks without flags, providing a clean baseline for further investigation.
